A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Memo research work. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices A.1–A.11, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on EXTOBJNAV, Dark-Key-To-Door, Memory Maze, and T-Maze, alongside ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a plot of Memo and RMT returns on T-Maze.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same summarization, memory accumulation, attention masking, positional encoding, segment randomization, and cache-refresh procedures. No algorithm or architecture component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions cover EXTOBJNAV, Dark-Key-To-Door, Memory Maze, and T-Maze. T-Maze was already evaluated in v1 Appendix A.7; its new plot does not establish additional task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain FCT, no-IEA, RMT, and the AC variants. The RMT comparator plotted in v2 Figure 8 was already compared with Memo in v1 A.7; the accompanying FCT discussion also remains.

E3.justification: The stated splits, metrics, training budgets, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Figure 8 newly specifies T-Maze length l=2000; v1 mentions 10,000 illustratively without unambiguously specifying the tested length, so an actual protocol change is not established.

E4.justification: The summary-length, segment-randomization, streaming, re-encoding, and training-validation analyses remain unchanged. A.7 already reports the T-Maze memory-accumulation diagnostic and its interpretation; v2 illustrates that existing analysis without introducing a new analytical test.

E5.justification: New Figure 8 displays shaded bands and error bars for the previously prose-only T-Maze comparison. Their statistical meaning and the T-Maze run count are unspecified. Existing seed statements are unchanged, and additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Figure 8 adds quantitative return trajectories for Memo and RMT at T-Maze length l=2000, showing higher later returns for Memo and unstable, lower RMT returns. The earlier 10× convergence-delay statement, all previously included plot images, and Table 1 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, positional-index expressions, reward definition, and SPL formula are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof, or formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about efficient learned memory, competitive or superior performance, long-context generalization, streaming robustness, and applicability to on-policy and off-policy RL.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations of accumulation, gradient propagation, re-encoding, and segment randomization are unchanged. The limitations concerning semantic generalization, memory consolidation, and context extrapolation are also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract newly states that code is available at gunshi/memo, while A.4 retains the early-release Memory-icrl/memo address and future-release wording. Figure 8 also documents l=2000. Other implementation details and the hyperparameter table are unchanged; repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The same 33 references and related-work positioning are retained, including the distinctions from Autocompressors, RMT, ReLIC, and AMAGO.

P1.justification: Edits include the code sentence, the affiliation change from Toyota Europe to Toyota Motor Europe, and figure-reference updates. The prose and section organization otherwise remain stable. A.6 incorrectly changes its Memory Maze reference from Figure 7 to Figure 8.

P2.justification: v2 adds the T-Maze plot as Figure 8, renumbers subsequent figures, and adjusts figure placement and page flow. Existing plot images and table structures are retained; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added T-Maze trajectories make a previously prose-only comparison inspectable, and the abstract makes code-access information more prominent. These are modest documentation gains. Undefined uncertainty bands, unreconciled code-release wording, and the incorrect Memory Maze cross-reference limit the improvement; the method and principal evidence remain unchanged.
